briefs.brief.md:
# Plotbook -- community garden plot booking

## Background
The Riverside Community Garden has 40 plots. Allocation is done today by a volunteer coordinator with paper forms and a wall chart. Plots are allocated per season (March to October).

## Users
- **Gardeners** (about 60 households) apply for a plot, see their allocation, and report a problem with their plot (broken tap, overgrown path).
- **The coordinator** (one volunteer) reviews applications, allocates plots, keeps a waiting list, and resolves reported problems.

## First version must
1. Let a gardener apply for a plot for the coming season, choosing up to three preferred plots.
2. Let the coordinator allocate plots from applications, and move unallocated applicants to a waiting list in application order.
3. Let a gardener see the plot allocated to them and the season dates.
4. Let a gardener report a problem with their plot; let the coordinator see open problems and mark them resolved.
5. Show the coordinator a plot map view (a grid of the 40 plots with who holds each).

## Rules
- A household holds at most one plot per season.
- Returning gardeners who held a plot last season are allocated before new applicants, if they apply before 1 February.
- The waiting list is strictly first come, first served.

## Later, not in the first version
- Online payment of the plot fee (paid in cash at the shed today).
- A shared tool-lending shelf.

## Constraints
- Must work on a phone; most gardeners apply from their phones.
- Gardener contact details are visible to the coordinator only.
- Must be usable by people who are not confident with technology: large text, plain language.

## Open questions
- How gardeners sign in has not been decided.
- Whether the coordinator is told about new problem reports, and how, has not been decided.

Phases represent demonstrable milestones; tickets are specific work items. After setup, `$story` loads this context for future sessions.

**Proposed assumptions**

- The coordinator maintains household records, with one sign-in email per household.
- Initial allocation opens on **1 February**, preserving priority for returning gardeners who apply before the cutoff.
- Preferences are optional, distinct, and not guaranteed. Waiting-list order cannot be bypassed through direct assignment or reassignment.
- Daily emails include newly reported problems, even if subsequently resolved; no email is sent when there are none.
- Garden timezone, exact season dates, and daily email time must be configured before launch.
- Framework and provider selection belongs to the foundation ticket; no technology is represented as already established.

**Ticket inventory**

These are provisional labels; Storybloq assigns permanent IDs during creation.

P01 and P02 can begin immediately after setup. Each implementation ticket includes scope, exclusions, observable acceptance, failure handling and verification. Checkpoints are ordinary tickets: Storybloq does **not yet enforce** their approval gates automatically.

The review findings are incorporated: allocation waits until the cutoff, roster/sign-in interfaces depend on prototype review, and FIFO protection covers assignment and reassignment.

SOURCE: brief.md
Plotbook serves Riverside Community Garden: 40 plots, about 60 households, one volunteer coordinator. Seasons March to October. First version: gardeners apply for coming season choosing up to 3 preferred plots; coordinator allocates from applications and moves unallocated applicants to a waiting list in application order; gardeners see allocated plot and season dates; gardeners report problems with their plot and coordinator views open problems/resolves them; coordinator sees grid of 40 plots and holders. Household at most one plot per season. Returning gardeners who held a plot last season allocated before new applicants if apply before 1 February. Waiting list strictly first come first served. Mobile, large text, plain language, contact details coordinator only. Later/excluded: payment and tool lending.
OWNER answers: emailed one-time links, no passwords; one email daily to coordinator listing new problem reports. No technology preference; exercise judgement on anything else. No implementation yet, no git, brief-only directory.

Product acceptance: all five first-version journeys with stated allocation, privacy and accessible mobile constraints plus link sign-in and daily digest. No claim of completed code.
Assumptions for approval: coordinator-managed household roster, one sign-in email per household in v1; coordinator can correct roster and historical occupancy so returning status is evidenced, not self-claimed. One plot per household AND one household per plot per season. Apply up to 3 distinct valid preferences, zero permitted. One application per household per season with idempotent retry; initial submitted timestamp preserved. Returning-priority applies to allocation, never reorders waiting list. Before Feb 1 means strictly earlier than Feb 1 00:00 in garden timezone. Exact season dates/timezone and digest time are coordinator configuration, not invented facts; no deploy until set. Returning priority is a category, not guarantee of same plot; within category use application timestamp + stable sequence ties. Coordinator selects among available plots (preferences not guaranteed). Waitlist promotion offers next FIFO household an available plot through coordinator confirmation; no self-service cancellation, offers/expiry or preference-based skipping in v1. Daily email uses new reports since last successful digest, including since-resolved reports labeled status, no empty digest; delivery failure must not discard reports. With provider idempotency support avoid duplicate deliveries; surface failures and permit safe retry, no impossible exactly-once claim.
Technology: do not lock a framework/vendor now. Project metadata Plotbook, generic, language TBD. P01 establishes implementation tools/provider choices and documents rationale; technical selection is delegated to implementer by owner. Planned single web app, relational persistence with transactional uniqueness, server-side authorization, email transport and durable daily job. No payment, tool lending, public holder directory, gardener admin interface, maps/geolocation.
